predecessors.name: Ottoman Tripolitania
predecessors.text: the Ottoman vilayets of Trablus (Tripoli) and Benghazi, whose military personnel withdrew under the Treaty of Ouchy of 18 October 1912

successors.name: British Africa
successors.text: Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, abandoned by the retreating German and Italian forces in February 1943 and administered by Britain

successors.name: Free France
successors.text: 'The Fezzan was occupied by the Free French in 1943'

ledger.x: 1911 (4 October): Italian forces land on the shores of Libya, and 'With a decree of 5 November 1911, Italy declared its sovereignty over Libya.'
1911 (4 October): the Italo-Turkish War reaches Libya.
1912 (18 October): the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war.
1912 (18 October): the Ottomans give up Libya.
1915 (by 1 August): Italy pulls back to the coast.
1916: Italy re-occupies Zuwarah (the page: 'with Zuwarah re-occupied in 1916').
1918 (16 November): the Tripolitanian Republic is proclaimed.
1923: the republic's land is back under Italy.
1923: Italy controls the Tripolitanian Republic's territory.
1923: the Second Italo-Senussi War begins.
1924: Sirtica is taken.
1928: the Ghibla falls.
1930: the Fezzan is conquered.
1931: Kufra is seized.
1932 (January): the last Cyrenaican resistance ends.
1932: Cyrenaica is Italian.
1934 (1 January): Tripolitania and Cyrenaica are unified.
1934 (20 July): the Sarra triangle goes to Libya.
1943: the Fezzan passes to Free France.
1943 (February): Libya is lost.
1943 (13 May): Italian rule in Libya ends.

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War
wars.outcome: Italian victory on paper: the Treaty of Ouchy of 18 October 1912; Italy held only the coastal enclaves and by 1 August 1915 had withdrawn from the interior.

wars.name: Italian reconquest of Tripolitania
wars.outcome: Italian victory: 'By 1923, Italian control was effective in the territories of the Republic'.

wars.name: Second Italo-Senussi War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: Sirtica 1924, Ghibla 1928, Fezzan 1930, Kufra 1931, Omar Mukhtar captured September 1931, campaign ended January 1932.

certainty.note: Italian control was by enclave and then by column along the coast, the Sirtica and the desert oases; the Egyptian line was finalised by the treaty of 6 December 1925 (ratified 1932-3) and demarcated in 1926-7, but nothing else is fixed.
The Sudan frontier is the Rome agreement of 20 July 1934; the Egyptian line was demarcated in 1926-7 and 1937-8.
